newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debts mixed, undertone firm.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debts mixed, undertone firm.

text.p: Emerging debt prices hovered around late Monday's level in moderate trading, traders said.
The bounce in the Treasuries and the U.S. stock market gave players renewed confidence that the rug would not be pulled from under the emerging debt, a U.S. bank trader said.

"People were relieved when the Dow bounced back nicely," he said. Wall Street stocks sold off on Monday amid concerns about a possible Japanese sale of U.S. Treasuries, resulting in a 192 point loss on the day. The Dow Industrials closed up 154 points on Tuesday.
Early jitters took a toll of high-yielders such as some Bulgaria and Ecuador issues, but general market tone was upbeat, traders said.
Ecuador PDI and Bulgaria FLRB were each off 1/2 to bid at 66-3/4 and 561/2.
The friendly U.S. interest rate environment is likely to encourage emerging market issuers to keep the summer calendar busy, said Walter Molano, Latin America economist at SBC/Warburg Securities.
"Venezuela is the most likely candidate for a swap or buyback deal, following the examples of Argentina, Brazil and Ecuador earlier this year," he said.
The Mexican elections in two weeks may cause some volatility in the short term, but investors appeared to be comfortable with longer dated papers, he said.
For example, one-year Cetes rate fell one percentage point to 22 percent since late May, he noted.
Mexico UMS 23, which lost 1-1/2 on Monday, regained 5/8 to bid at 114-3/4.
Outside Latin America, Poland attracted investors' attention with its new Yankee, which is to be launched soon, said another trader.
"Every time you get a new Eurobond or Yankee, the old Bradys go up," he said, adding that PDI bond at this moment held the most allure.
Poland Pars was off 1/8 at 86-7/8 bid.
